## This game

A new game. You play Black, so you move first.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: `read_file(path)` and `list_files(path)` to read, and `apply_patch` to create, change and delete any file in your working directory.

You may write and run code. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I’ll read the last two reviews, keep the opponent at 20k, and count Black’s area target early. I’ll preserve the move responses and leave a review for game 82.

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.

function replay(moves, snapshots, inspect) {
 const cols="ABCDEFGHJ", b={}, captures={B:0,W:0}, history=[], captureEvents=[];
 for(const c of cols)for(let y=1;y<=9;y++)b[c+y]=".";
 const ns=p=>{const x=cols.indexOf(p[0]),y=+p[1];return [[x-1,y],[x+1,y],[x,y-1],[x,y+1]].filter(([a,c])=>a>=0&&a<9&&c>=1&&c<=9).map(([a,c])=>cols[a]+c);};
 const group=p=>{const q=[p],seen=new Set(q),libs=new Set();while(q.length){const a=q.pop();for(const n of ns(a)){if(b[n]===b[p]&&!seen.has(n)){seen.add(n);q.push(n);}else if(b[n]===".")libs.add(n);}}return {stones:[...seen].sort(),liberties:[...libs].sort()};};
 let ko=null;
 for(const m of moves){
  const stone=m.color==="B"?"X":"O",enemy=stone==="X"?"O":"X",removed=[];
  if(m.move==="pass")ko=null;
  else {
   if(b[m.move]!=="."||m.move===ko)throw Error("illegal actual move "+m.number);
   b[m.move]=stone;

   const own=group(m.move);if(!own.liberties.length)throw Error("actual suicide "+m.number);
   ko=removed.length===1&&own.stones.length===1&&own.liberties.length===1?removed[0]:null;
   captures[m.color]+=removed.length;
   if(removed.length)captureEvents.push({number:m.number,color:m.color,move:m.move,removed:removed.sort(),ko});
  }
  history.push({position:m.number,move:m,board:{...b},captures:{...captures},ko});
 }

  const t=s.result.content.filter(c=>c.type==="text").map(c=>c.text).join("\n");
  const match=t.match(/Move number: (\d+)/), position=+match[1]-1, state=history[position-1], actual=inspect(t).board;

const movesText=load("moves").map(m=>`${m.number} ${m.color} ${m.move}`).join(", ");
const review=`# Game 81: Black vs 20k — W+2

Played 2026-10-06. 9×9, Chinese area scoring, komi 7, simple ko.
Black53/White54 passes ended the game; board() confirmed W+2.
Independent area Black43/White38+7, physical captures Black2/White1, dead0/neutral0.
All final stones survived: Black lower13 stones scored29; upper12 scored14.
20k record: fifteen wins, fifty-nine losses, three draws. Retain20k.

## Records and verification

Read80/79 and consulted30 before choosing20k.
game-081.sgf records all54 actual moves. game-081-log.json preserves selection, all27 play responses, final confirmation, exact moves, target, inventories and actual-history replay.
All54 moves replayed legally; 29 complete snapshots (initial,27 play responses,confirmation) matched boards, capture totals, move numbers and ko markers.
Every scratch mutation was explicitly stored. No raw response was lost.
Black27 turns−onepass−one captured=25; White27−fourpasses−two captured=21.
Full current inspections executed after32 and52; groups inspected after40 and48. Other snapshot inspections in the JSON were added retrospectively.
Code inspected supplied boards, replayed actual recorded history and kept records only. Choices and hypothetical reading were manual; no engine, Monte Carlo, future-sequence search or move selection/ranking/recommendation.
No invalid move, ko, resignation or dead removal. No optimal opening, winning replacement, individual move values or exhaustive invasion proof established.
Game52's unresolved scoring discrepancy remains separate.

## Exact moves

${movesText}.

## Timely counting, inadequate reduction margin

C3/G7/G3 selected the lower and upper-right bases. White E5/C6/G5 took central influence.
E3 broadened the lower boundary; C4 met WhiteD4.
After move10 the exact disjoint target was executed:
all nine columns rows1–3 =27;
A4/B4/C4 =3;
G/H/J rows4–9 excluding current WhiteG5 =17;
total47.

Five Black stones existed, with no enclosed empty room or completed eye proof. All47 selected points remained conditional.
Immediate caps included C6/D4/E5/G5/E7. Missing lower joins D3/F3, right routes, first-line endpoints and eye dividers competed for turns.
Black requires45 if all81 assigned: the target had only two points of reduction margin.
The arithmetic was timely and accurate; this did not make the framework sufficient.

D3 at11 joined C3/E3; F3 at13 joined E3/G3, creating one lower chain.
H5 at15 was initially separate, with H4/H6/J5 three liberties.
WhiteG6 reduced47 to46; H6 joinedH5, and H7 joined those stones toG7.
WhiteH4 at20 reduced46 to45, leaving no margin.
H3 at21 joinedG3 and prevented a direct enemy extension into that selected lower point.
WhiteG4 at22 reduced45 to44.

The deficit was explicitly recognized, but there was no successful strategic broadening that restored a winning margin.
G8/G9 retained the upper endpoint against F8/E9 caps.
WhiteJ4 removed another selected point =>43.
J3 secured the lower first-line endpoint.
WhiteB4/A4 removed two more =>41; B3/A3 joined and retained the lower row3 boundary.
F9 at33 and F4 at35 were genuine joined gains outside the original target =>43.
WhiteE9/E4 capped further direct growth. Neither move at those points was claimed to be an ignored-atari capture.

This differs from game80's additional eleven-area living base: only two outside points were acquired.
Recognizing the deficit is insufficient unless it changes development while useful room remains.
No specific earlier order or alternate opening was verified to win.

## Upper captures: preserve the main's liberties and join J8

J5 at37 retained the upper group's lower endpoint.
WhiteJ7 at38 had J6/J8 two liberties.
BlackJ8 at39 ataried it at soleJ6, but J8 was isolated with H8/J9 two own liberties.
WhiteH9 at40 had H8/J9 two liberties.
The eight-stone main then had H8/J6 only; separate J8 also had H8/J9.
Do not infer safety from the enemy's atari alone.

H8 at41 joined J8/main and ataried H9 at soleJ9.
The joined main had J6/J9 two liberties; White passed.
J9 at43 captured H9 and joined through J8. Main liberties became H9/J6, two; no ko.
White passed again.
J6 at45 captured J7 and joined H6/J5. Main liberties became H9/J7, two; no ko.

Final true eyes:
H9 bounded by G9/H8/J9;
J7 bounded by H7/J6/J8.
All boundary stones are in the same twelve-stone upper group.
Both captures restored selected H9/J7; neither added outside area.
The captures followed ignored ataris/passes, but J6 was already an impossible White self-extension while the main retained its other liberty.
No unverified remote rescue was counted. Leave both eyes empty.

## Failed B5 threat: opposing groups shared A5

Before Black47, WhiteA4/B4 had A5/B5.
BlackB5 at47 had soleA5, because B4/B6/C5 were White.
It ataried A4/B4 at the same soleA5.
This was a knowingly vulnerable one-stone attempt to gain area if ignored, not a forced capture or life plan.
WhiteA5 at48 correctly captured B5 before checking its own liberties.
The resulting WhiteA4/A5/B4 group had A6/B5 TWO liberties. No ko.
The vacated B5 was a new enemy liberty, so a Black recapture could not capture that group.

The threat failed. The final score ledger gained no points from it.
Do not treat an atari sharing the attacker's last liberty as a forced gain, or rely on the opponent repeating earlier passes.
The move did not endanger either established Black framework, but it was not a verified solution to the deficit.
No general individual move value is assigned from this outcome.

## Lower life and final score

E2 at49 joinedE3; E1 at51 extended to the first line and divided the lower eighteen-point room.
Two separate eight-point spaces remained:
A1/A2/B1/B2/C1/C2/D1/D2;
F1/F2/G1/G2/H1/H2/J1/J2.
All boundaries belong to the thirteen-stone lower group. These are large eye rooms, not sixteen individual true eyes.
Official scoring retained every stone; no exhaustive invasion analysis was performed.
The divider added no area. WhiteD8/D6 stayed outside the selected Black outline.

Exact target47 loses A4/B4/G4/G6/H4/J4 six =>41, gainsF4/F9 two =>43.
Upper original17 losesG4/G6/H4/J4 four =>13, gainsF9=>14.
Lower original30 losesA4/B4 two =>28, gainsF4=>29.
The H9/J7 captures restored original points and are not added again.

Black25 stones+18 territory=43:
upper12+H9/J7 two=14;
lower13+two eight-point rooms=29.
White21 stones+17 territory=38:
A6/A7/A8/A9/B7/B8/B9/C7/C8/C9/D7/D9 twelve;
E8 one; E6/F6 two; B5 one; D5 one.
No dead or neutral points.
White38+7−Black43=2, matching the official W+2.
One White-to-Black coordinate shift draws; two win. This is arithmetic, not a valuation of particular moves.

After the executed position52 inspection, Black53 passed and White54 passed.

## Carry forward

Retain20k; next read81/80 and consult30 for broad development.
Count early, but assess whether remaining joins/endpoints/dividers can withstand immediate caps. Game81's47 lost six and gained two; merely declaring an area deficit did not change that result.
Broaden connected viable room before it closes. This game establishes no winning alternate order.
Separate genuine gains (F4/F9) from restored targets (H9/J7) and internal life moves (H8/E2/E1).
Check the main and capturer together: J8 needed H8's prompt join while the main had only two liberties.
Reject a shared-last-liberty atari as a forced capture: WhiteA5 correctly capturedB5 and reopenedB5.
Store scratch arrays after mutation; all raw snapshots were preserved and verified this time.
`;
store("review",review);
text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: game-081.md\n"+review.trimEnd().split("\n").map(l=>"+"+l).join("\n")+"\n*** End Patch"));

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
